![](images/c6/c682f99e66e12fb124beaee9ae090978444e402b74ce675f0eb2f7939c1ed06d.svg)
What is the missing expression?" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186198392 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-5b08ff1d-1edf-523c-a8e8-287f135b6040" "question-431ed508-ca53-50c3-b7a4-875fc9b23084"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-ef91d27f-5ce3-5c48-b5b9-4ec732b3b2e1" :question/id #uuid "ef91d27f-5ce3-5c48-b5b9-4ec732b3b2e1" :question/math-academy-id "q-161471" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x-3y$ for $-1\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-3v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-de6e4169-2fd0-5a0b-b7fe-172964aca58f"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-de6e4169-2fd0-5a0b-b7fe-172964aca58f" :answer-field/id #uuid "de6e4169-2fd0-5a0b-b7fe-172964aca58f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-9d9623af-3bba-5a0d-9c01-61a215703653" :answer-field/choices ["answer-86aaa33f-073f-5b9c-b6ed-02e42f1370d2" "answer-9d9623af-3bba-5a0d-9c01-61a215703653" "answer-8fa80cac-9ed0-54f2-a0fb-a71697486081" "answer-556660a7-ba40-5142-a23c-96cdb3bb38b3" "answer-b721d1da-8cb3-5423-bdff-f515271a77db"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-86aaa33f-073f-5b9c-b6ed-02e42f1370d2" :answer/id #uuid "86aaa33f-073f-5b9c-b6ed-02e42f1370d2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12u-v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9d9623af-3bba-5a0d-9c01-61a215703653" :answer/id #uuid "9d9623af-3bba-5a0d-9c01-61a215703653" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5u-17v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8fa80cac-9ed0-54f2-a0fb-a71697486081" :answer/id #uuid "8fa80cac-9ed0-54f2-a0fb-a71697486081" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8u+14v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-556660a7-ba40-5142-a23c-96cdb3bb38b3" :answer/id #uuid "556660a7-ba40-5142-a23c-96cdb3bb38b3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8u-23v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b721d1da-8cb3-5423-bdff-f515271a77db" :answer/id #uuid "b721d1da-8cb3-5423-bdff-f515271a77db" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "u-6v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186198593 :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $-2\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186194189 :answer-field/correct "answer-63293960-e3b1-529e-96e9-642aedf596e5" :answer-field/choices ["answer-cb8fdbef-d72d-513a-8e44-4a96d82e4382" "answer-e83e93b0-2e8f-5324-b1ed-23d683ac8523" "answer-1cea6d00-8d2b-5733-8616-9267687fd149" "answer-63293960-e3b1-529e-96e9-642aedf596e5" "answer-84b21f44-ef97-5299-8654-bb5534b15960"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cb8fdbef-d72d-513a-8e44-4a96d82e4382" :answer/id #uuid "cb8fdbef-d72d-513a-8e44-4a96d82e4382" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2{u}^{2}v-uv+{v}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e83e93b0-2e8f-5324-b1ed-23d683ac8523" :answer/id #uuid "e83e93b0-2e8f-5324-b1ed-23d683ac8523" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "u+v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1cea6d00-8d2b-5733-8616-9267687fd149" :answer/id #uuid "1cea6d00-8d2b-5733-8616-9267687fd149" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "uv+v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-63293960-e3b1-529e-96e9-642aedf596e5" :answer/id #uuid "63293960-e3b1-529e-96e9-642aedf596e5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "uv-v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-84b21f44-ef97-5299-8654-bb5534b15960" :answer/id #uuid "84b21f44-ef97-5299-8654-bb5534b15960" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{u}^{2}+uv+{v}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-92e8ddd2-ccb6-5c20-b74b-2f784e857a55" :question/id #uuid "92e8ddd2-ccb6-5c20-b74b-2f784e857a55" :question/math-academy-id "q-161379" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=y-x$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $-3\le y\le 0.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1+(u-v)^{2}\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =5uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}5uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-dce1231b-682c-5119-8b60-1e600b81511c"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $F(x,y,z)=⟨{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,{y}^{2}-{z}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=-x-y$ for $-2\le x\le 2$ and $-2\le y\le 2.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,-u-v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 2,\,-2\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,{y}^{2}-{z}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=-u-v} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2},\,(-u-v)^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2},\,(-u-v)^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot (1)+({v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2})\cdot (1)+(-u-v)^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}+{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2}+(-u-v)^{2} \\  & ={u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,{y}^{2}-{z}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,4u-v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=4u-v} \\  & =⟨2u-(4u-v),\,v-(4u-v),\,4u-v+v⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\cdot ⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(-2u+v)\cdot (-4)+(-4u+2v)\cdot 1+4u\cdot 1 \\  & =8u-4v+-4u+2v+4u \\  & =8u-2v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(8u-2v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(8u-2v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-5b08ff1d-1edf-523c-a8e8-287f135b6040" :question/id #uuid "5b08ff1d-1edf-523c-a8e8-287f135b6040" :question/math-academy-id "q-162607" :question/problem "For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186401240 :question/problem "For a surface $S$ given by $y=2x{z}^{3}$ for $(x,z)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

*Hint: The orientation of $S$ should be chosen such that the unit normal vector has a positive  $j$-component.*" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186199473 :tutorial/content "Let's calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle (x-y)^2, \:(x+y)^2, \: 12xy \right\rangle
$$

 

through the surface $S$ defined by the Cartesian equation 

$$
z=2y-2x
$$

for $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$ 

For surfaces like this, substituting $x=u$ and $y=v,$ we obtain a parametrization 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: 2v-2u \right\rangle
$$

over the domain 

$$
D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 1, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

 

Recall that for a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2v-2u} \\  & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\cdot ⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)^{2}\cdot 2+(u+v)^{2}\cdot (-2)+12uv\cdot 1 \\  & =4uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}4uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =[{u}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})\cdot ({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186199470 :tutorial/content "Let's now derive a general formula for the flux through an *upward-oriented* Cartesian surface.

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Consider a surface $S$ given by the equation $z=g(x,y).$ The canonical parameterization of the surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle.
$$

Computing the tangent vectors to the grid curves, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$

$$

Notice that the $\mathbf k$-component is positive, which indicates that our surface is upward-oriented.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize as follows:

- *For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} - Q\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \right) \textrm{d}A.
$$

We have analogous results for surfaces of the form $y = h(x,z)$ and $x=k(y,z){:}$

- *For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} + Q - R\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf j$-component is positive.*

- *For a surface $S$ given $x = k(y,z)$ for $(y,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( P - Q\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial y} - R\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf i$-component is positive.*" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186198485 :activity/expected-seconds 1020.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-3v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-de6e4169-2fd0-5a0b-b7fe-172964aca58f"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-de6e4169-2fd0-5a0b-b7fe-172964aca58f" :answer-field/id #uuid "de6e4169-2fd0-5a0b-b7fe-172964aca58f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-9d9623af-3bba-5a0d-9c01-61a215703653" :answer-field/choices ["answer-86aaa33f-073f-5b9c-b6ed-02e42f1370d2" "answer-9d9623af-3bba-5a0d-9c01-61a215703653" "answer-8fa80cac-9ed0-54f2-a0fb-a71697486081" "answer-556660a7-ba40-5142-a23c-96cdb3bb38b3" "answer-b721d1da-8cb3-5423-bdff-f515271a77db"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-86aaa33f-073f-5b9c-b6ed-02e42f1370d2" :answer/id #uuid "86aaa33f-073f-5b9c-b6ed-02e42f1370d2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12u-v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9d9623af-3bba-5a0d-9c01-61a215703653" :answer/id #uuid "9d9623af-3bba-5a0d-9c01-61a215703653" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5u-17v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8fa80cac-9ed0-54f2-a0fb-a71697486081" :answer/id #uuid "8fa80cac-9ed0-54f2-a0fb-a71697486081" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8u+14v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-556660a7-ba40-5142-a23c-96cdb3bb38b3" :answer/id #uuid "556660a7-ba40-5142-a23c-96cdb3bb38b3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8u-23v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b721d1da-8cb3-5423-bdff-f515271a77db" :answer/id #uuid "b721d1da-8cb3-5423-bdff-f515271a77db" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "u-6v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186198593 :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $-2\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,{y}^{2}-{z}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=-u-v} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2},\,(-u-v)^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2},\,(-u-v)^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot (1)+({v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2})\cdot (1)+(-u-v)^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}+{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2}+(-u-v)^{2} \\  & ={u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,{y}^{2}-{z}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-2bbc92cc-19ad-54ee-9d42-9ce995a00f4a"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-2bbc92cc-19ad-54ee-9d42-9ce995a00f4a" :answer-field/id #uuid "2bbc92cc-19ad-54ee-9d42-9ce995a00f4a" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-146aebe7-02b6-58b6-8dd1-374b1fcd30d0" :answer-field/choices ["answer-6197b42b-5e97-5e6b-a1bb-2951dc50be38" "answer-cacced8e-053e-5057-89f0-678a72c14a18" "answer-3586c1bc-3061-5093-99ca-95e798991986" "answer-146aebe7-02b6-58b6-8dd1-374b1fcd30d0" "answer-5a1a3ab5-07e2-55d2-b713-d20c37bdda9e"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6197b42b-5e97-5e6b-a1bb-2951dc50be38" :answer/id #uuid "6197b42b-5e97-5e6b-a1bb-2951dc50be38" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2uv" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cacced8e-053e-5057-89f0-678a72c14a18" :answer/id #uuid "cacced8e-053e-5057-89f0-678a72c14a18" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3v" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3586c1bc-3061-5093-99ca-95e798991986" :answer/id #uuid "3586c1bc-3061-5093-99ca-95e798991986" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4uv" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-146aebe7-02b6-58b6-8dd1-374b1fcd30d0" :answer/id #uuid "146aebe7-02b6-58b6-8dd1-374b1fcd30d0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{u}^{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5a1a3ab5-07e2-55d2-b713-d20c37bdda9e" :answer/id #uuid "5a1a3ab5-07e2-55d2-b713-d20c37bdda9e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{u}^{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186373986 :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,4u-v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=4u-v} \\  & =⟨2u-(4u-v),\,v-(4u-v),\,4u-v+v⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\cdot ⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(-2u+v)\cdot (-4)+(-4u+2v)\cdot 1+4u\cdot 1 \\  & =8u-4v+-4u+2v+4u \\  & =8u-2v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(8u-2v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(8u-2v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-5b08ff1d-1edf-523c-a8e8-287f135b6040" :question/id #uuid "5b08ff1d-1edf-523c-a8e8-287f135b6040" :question/math-academy-id "q-162607" :question/problem "For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186401240 :question/problem "For a surface $S$ given by $y=2x{z}^{3}$ for $(x,z)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,{z}^{3}+Q-\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,x{z}^{2})\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

*Hint: The orientation of $S$ should be chosen such that the unit normal vector has a positive  $j$-component.*" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186199473 :tutorial/content "Let's calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle (x-y)^2, \:(x+y)^2, \: 12xy \right\rangle
$$

 

through the surface $S$ defined by the Cartesian equation 

$$
z=2y-2x
$$

for $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$ 

For surfaces like this, substituting $x=u$ and $y=v,$ we obtain a parametrization 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: 2v-2u \right\rangle
$$

over the domain 

$$
D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 1, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

 

Recall that for a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2v-2u} \\  & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\cdot ⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)^{2}\cdot 2+(u+v)^{2}\cdot (-2)+12uv\cdot 1 \\  & =4uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}4uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =[{u}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})\cdot ({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186199470 :tutorial/content "Let's now derive a general formula for the flux through an *upward-oriented* Cartesian surface.

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Consider a surface $S$ given by the equation $z=g(x,y).$ The canonical parameterization of the surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle.
$$

Computing the tangent vectors to the grid curves, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the $\mathbf k$-component is positive, which indicates that our surface is upward-oriented.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize as follows:

- *For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} - Q\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \right) \textrm{d}A.
$$

We have analogous results for surfaces of the form $y = h(x,z)$ and $x=k(y,z){:}$

- *For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} + Q - R\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf j$-component is positive.*

- *For a surface $S$ given $x = k(y,z)$ for $(y,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( P - Q\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial y} - R\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

What is the missing expression?"] ["question-ef91d27f-5ce3-5c48-b5b9-4ec732b3b2e1" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-3v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-ef91d27f-5ce3-5c48-b5b9-4ec732b3b2e1" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-de6e4169-2fd0-5a0b-b7fe-172964aca58f" :answer-field/id #uuid $$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}

{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1+(u-v)^{2}\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =5uv.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,-u-v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 2,\,-2\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,{y}^{2}-{z}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=-u-v} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2},\,(-u-v)^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2},\,(-u-v)^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot (1)+({v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2})\cdot (1)+(-u-v)^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}+{v}^{2}-(-u-v)^{2}+(-u-v)^{2} \\  & ={u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,{y}^{2}-{z}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-29805411-7a4c-51f7-893d-a0f3dc3cef10" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-2bbc92cc-19ad-54ee-9d42-9ce995a00f4a" :answer-field/id #uuid $$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\cdot ⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(-2u+v)\cdot (-4)+(-4u+2v)\cdot 1+4u\cdot 1 \\  & =8u-4v+-4u+2v+4u \\  & =8u-2v.\end{aligned}

*Hint: The orientation of $S$ should be chosen such that the unit normal vector has a positive  $j$-component.*"] [17592186199473 :tutorial/content "Let's calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle (x-y)^2, \:(x+y)^2, \: 12xy \right\rangle
$$

 

through the surface $S$ defined by the Cartesian equation 

$$
z=2y-2x
$$

for $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$ 

For surfaces like this, substituting $x=u$ and $y=v,$ we obtain a parametrization 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: 2v-2u \right\rangle
$$

over the domain 

$$
D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 1, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

 

Recall that for a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2v-2u} \\  & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\cdot ⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)^{2}\cdot 2+(u+v)^{2}\cdot (-2)+12uv\cdot 1 \\  & =4uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}4uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =[{u}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})\cdot ({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$"] [17592186199470 :tutorial/content "Let's now derive a general formula for the flux through an *upward-oriented* Cartesian surface.

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Consider a surface $S$ given by the equation $z=g(x,y).$ The canonical parameterization of the surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle.
$$

Computing the tangent vectors to the grid curves, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the $\mathbf k$-component is positive, which indicates that our surface is upward-oriented.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize as follows:

- *For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} - Q\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \right) \textrm{d}A.
$$

We have analogous results for surfaces of the form $y = h(x,z)$ and $x=k(y,z){:}$

- *For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} + Q - R\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf j$-component is positive.*

- *For a surface $S$ given $x = k(y,z)$ for $(y,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( P - Q\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial y} - R\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Consider a surface $S$ given by the equation $z=g(x,y).$ The canonical parameterization of the surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle.
$$

Computing the tangent vectors to the grid curves, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{'} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{'} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{'}\times {r}_{y}^{'} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the $\mathbf k$-component is positive, which indicates that our surface is upward-oriented.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{'}\times {r}_{y}^{'})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize as follows:

- *For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} - Q\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \right) \textrm{d}A.
$$

We have analogous results for surfaces of the form $y = h(x,z)$ and $x=k(y,z){:}$

- *For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} + Q - R\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf j$-component is positive.*

- *For a surface $S$ given $x = k(y,z)$ for $(y,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( P - Q\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial y} - R\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf i$-component is positive.*"]]}

$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨xy,\,x+y,\,{e}^{z}⟩{|}_{z=x+y} \\  & =⟨xy,\,x+y,\,{e}^{x+y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{{xy}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{x+y}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{{e}^{x+y}}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨xy,\,x+y,\,{e}^{z}⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(xy)\cdot 1-(x+y)\cdot 1+{e}^{x+y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-xy-x-y+{e}^{x+y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}(-xy-x-y+{e}^{x+y})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-\frac{x{y}^{2}}{2}-xy-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+{e}^{x+y}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}-{x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{e}^{2x}-{e}^{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}+{e}^{2x}-{e}^{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{{x}^{4}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}-{e}^{x}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(-\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}-e)-(0+\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{2}-8e-1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186278522 :question/id #uuid "da0b12bf-561c-5907-8348-62e84bca5b63" :question/math-academy-id "q-161481" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186198379 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "aaa6b152-86d3-5f96-8a94-57f86a17a84d" :knowledge-point/title "Evaluating Flux Over a Surface"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "15f8ea45-7189-5de7-b023-513085bc87a0" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\pi +\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{3}" :db/id 17592186275684} {:answer/id #uuid "1d8d5990-f27c-5d2a-8556-ade0d064ae64" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\pi -\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{6}" :db/id 17592186275747} {:answer/id #uuid "9b81db63-fffe-50ae-abb4-769c30bdcdcc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\pi +\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{12}" :db/id 17592186276871} {:answer/id #uuid "bb7a2355-821a-5abf-ae21-cfb859e97e99" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\pi }{4}" :db/id 17592186277145} {:answer/id #uuid "e9752611-528c-5fdc-8927-863cf9474421" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\pi }{2}" :db/id 17592186277518}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "1d8d5990-f27c-5d2a-8556-ade0d064ae64" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\pi -\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{6}" :db/id 17592186275747} :answer-field/id #uuid "6db629ff-d6ea-571f-9225-53d34e230d79" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186277919}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487 :db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/problem "Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y) \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨1,\,0,\,y⟩{|}_{z=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)} \\  & =⟨{{1}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{0}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{y}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨1,\,0,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y))-0\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y))+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{0}{\int }_{-x}^{0}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)+y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{0}{[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=-x}^{y=0}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{0}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+0)-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡0+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{0}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\operatorname{sin}⁡x+x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}]}_{-\pi }^{0} \\  & =0-(-0+(-\pi )-\frac{(-\pi )^{3}}{6}) \\  & =\pi -\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{6}\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186278545 :question/id #uuid "d858f67e-e87d-5922-848f-1cf10db83bc5" :question/math-academy-id "q-161536"} {:db/id 17592186278546 :question/id #uuid 17592186045486 :db/ident :question.difficulty/hard} :question/problem "Calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨x+y,\,y-x,\,z⟩,
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $-1\le y\le 1.$" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2y\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the flux of $F$ through $S$ is given by 

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨x+y,\,y-x,\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨x+y,\,y-x,\,z⟩{|}_{z=1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =⟨{{x+y}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{y-x}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨x+y,\,y-x,\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(x+y)\cdot (2x)-(y-x)\cdot (2y)+1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2{x}^{2}-2xy-2{y}^{2}+2xy+1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{[y-{x}^{2}y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=-1}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[(1-{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{3})-(-1+{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3})]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(2-2{x}^{2}-\frac{2}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2x-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{2}{3}x]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(2-\frac{2}{3}-\frac{2}{3})-(-2+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186278551 :question/id #uuid "d0720c99-cc1f-5800-96bf-793fcc7002e7" :question/math-academy-id "q-161552"} {:db/id 17592186373972 :question/id #uuid "9a86f1df-9194-5ee6-ac19-2bfbeca02663" :question/math-academy-id "q-161447" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186198379 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "aaa6b152-86d3-5f96-8a94-57f86a17a84d" :knowledge-point/title "Evaluating Flux Over a Surface"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "35f2e086-31b9-544a-9b9a-99a08a27f04e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{7}{2}" :db/id 17592186373974} {:answer/id #uuid "291af077-cf81-5322-8799-9c4d0a56816f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{5}{2}" :db/id 17592186373975} {:answer/id #uuid "84fcb1f0-4936-5fbf-afb7-a71a059f4960" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186373976} {:answer/id #uuid "c8544813-339e-5ed8-a745-c0b3a602e975" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "1" :db/id 17592186373977} {:answer/id #uuid "c730413b-a101-500a-a942-8a345613f8ae" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0" :db/id 17592186373978}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "291af077-cf81-5322-8799-9c4d0a56816f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{5}{2}" :db/id 17592186373975} :answer-field/id #uuid "05d45f19-fa05-53a9-92e1-77a6078e07fb" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186373973}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487 :db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/problem "Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨y,\,x+z,\,z+2x⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=y-2x$ for $1\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 1.$" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-2x)=-2 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2x)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨y,\,x+z,\,z+2x⟩{|}_{z=y-2x} \\  & =⟨y,\,x+(y-2x),\,y-2x+2x⟩ \\  & =⟨{{y}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{y-x}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{y}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨y,\,x+z,\,z+2x⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y\cdot (-2)-(y-x)\cdot (1)+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y-y+x+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y+x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2y+x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[{y}^{2}+xy]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(1+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[x+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2+2-1-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186401261 :question/id #uuid "682d2ef7-9cff-5a52-921d-70cd49bbb080" :question/math-academy-id "q-161476"} {:db/id 17592186198389 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id Integral"}] :question/problem "Consider the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle z+2y, \: 3y+z, \: x -z\right\rangle$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=-3x+2y$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ can be expressed as
![](images/37/3761b12939f74f1e7f4d01ca83ea2884c1296672e22128064b109f7c42bb4df6.png)
What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: -3u+2v \right\rangle
$$

over the domain 

$$
D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 2, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-3u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-3u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z+2y,\,3y+z,\,x-z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=-3u+2v} \\  & =⟨(-3u+2v)+2v,\,3v+(-3u+2v),\,u-(-3u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3u+4v,\,-3u+5v,\,4u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-3u+4v,\,-3u+5v,\,4u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨3,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(-3u+4v)\cdot (3)+(-3u+5v)\cdot (-2)+(4u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-9u+12v+6u-10v+4u-2v \\  & =u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z+2y,\,3y+z,\,x-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}u\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}u\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

17592186045485 :db/ident :question.difficulty/easy} :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=4x-y$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 2.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,4u-v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 2}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=4u-v} \\  & =⟨2u-(4u-v),\,v-(4u-v),\,4u-v+v⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\cdot ⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(-2u+v)\cdot (-4)+(-4u+2v)\cdot 1+4u\cdot 1 \\  & =8u-4v+-4u+2v+4u \\  & =8u-2v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(8u-2v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(8u-2v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186398514 :question/id #uuid "eec4b66c-4af6-5b13-942b-337cb7b8732a" :question/math-academy-id "q-161357"} {:db/id 17592186398521 :question/id #uuid $$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D 
\Bigg( 
\bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}} \dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} 
+ Q

$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

*Hint: The orientation of $S$ should be chosen such that the unit normal vector has a positive  $\mathbf j$-component.*" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $y = h(x,z),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,z) = \left\langle x, \: h(x,z),\: z \right\rangle.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,\frac{∂h}{∂x},\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨0,\frac{∂h}{∂z},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \frac{∂h}{∂x} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{∂h}{∂z} & 1\end{aligned}|=⟨\frac{∂h}{∂x},\,-1,\,\frac{∂h}{∂z}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

However, notice that the $\mathbf j$-component is negative. Therefore, we select the normal vector that points in the *opposite* direction:

$$
\mathbf{r}'_z \times \mathbf{r}'_x = - \mathbf{r}'_x \times \mathbf{r}'_z =   \left \langle -\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x}, \: 1, \: -\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right \rangle
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,z))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂h}{∂x},\,1,\,-\frac{∂h}{∂z}⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂h}{∂x}+Q-R\frac{∂h}{∂z})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186049883} {:db/id 17592186198602 :question/id #uuid "9923f940-6e67-51d8-8336-d46f1ce02fd1" :question/math-academy-id "q-161166"} {:db/id 17592186198605 :question/id #uuid $$

:step/math-academy-id 44446 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199282}} {:db/id 17592186199300 :step/content {:db/id 17592186199470 :tutorial/content "Let's now derive a general formula for the flux through an *upward-oriented* Cartesian surface.

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Consider a surface $S$ given by the equation $z=g(x,y).$ The canonical parameterization of the surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle.
$$

Computing the tangent vectors to the grid curves, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{'} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{'} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{'}\times {r}_{y}^{'} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the $\mathbf k$-component is positive, which indicates that our surface is upward-oriented.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{'}\times {r}_{y}^{'})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize as follows:

- *For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} - Q\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \right) \textrm{d}A.
$$

We have analogous results for surfaces of the form $y = h(x,z)$ and $x=k(y,z){:}$

- *For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} + Q - R\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf j$-component is positive.*

- *For a surface $S$ given $x = k(y,z)$ for $(y,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( P - Q\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial y} - R\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf i$-component is positive.*" :tutorial/id #uuid "d20203b0-e15f-5061-ae68-16676ec933dc" :tutorial/math-academy-id 7653 :tutorial/title "Formulas for Flux Over Cartesian Surfaces"} :step/id #uuid "299c6f48-c761-519a-8d96-161fea9d6df0" :step/math-academy-id 44449 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199299}} {:db/id 17592186199306 :step/content {:db/id 17592186199473 :tutorial/content "Let's calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle (x-y)^2, \:(x+y)^2, \: 12xy \right\rangle
$$

 

through the surface $S$ defined by the Cartesian equation 

$$
z=2y-2x
$$

for $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$ 

For surfaces like this, substituting $x=u$ and $y=v,$ we obtain a parametrization 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: 2v-2u \right\rangle
$$

over the domain 

$$
D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 1, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

 

Recall that for a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{'} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{'} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{'}\times {r}_{v}^{'} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2v-2u} \\  & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{'}\times {r}_{v}^{'})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}4uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =[{u}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})\cdot ({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "f32d6993-cd62-5fe7-98f3-9a89a815dbfc" :tutorial/math-academy-id 7666 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "dd32837c-4771-57ff-abbc-360334e17eeb" :step/math-academy-id 44522 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199295}}] :activity/title "Calculating Flux Through Cartesian Surfaces" :activity/type {:db/id 17592186045463 :db/ident :activity.type/lesson} :db/id 17592186198485} {:db/id 17592186199306 :step/content {:db/id 17592186199473 :tutorial/content "Let's calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{'} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{'} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Consider a surface $S$ given by the equation $z=g(x,y).$ The canonical parameterization of the surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle.
$$

Computing the tangent vectors to the grid curves, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{'} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{'} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{'}\times {r}_{y}^{'} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the $\mathbf k$-component is positive, which indicates that our surface is upward-oriented.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{'}\times {r}_{y}^{'})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize as follows:

- *For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} - Q\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \right) \textrm{d}A.
$$

We have analogous results for surfaces of the form $y = h(x,z)$ and $x=k(y,z){:}$

- *For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} + Q - R\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf j$-component is positive.*

- *For a surface $S$ given $x = k(y,z)$ for $(y,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( P - Q\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial y} - R\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf i$-component is positive.*" :tutorial/id #uuid "d20203b0-e15f-5061-ae68-16676ec933dc" :tutorial/math-academy-id 7653 :tutorial/title "Formulas for Flux Over Cartesian Surfaces"} :step/id #uuid "299c6f48-c761-519a-8d96-161fea9d6df0" :step/math-academy-id 44449 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199299}} {:db/id 17592186199299 :step/content {:db/id 17592186198392 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186198034 :question/id #uuid "b81eb0cb-a740-5e86-921c-4baa8c179e55" :question/math-academy-id "e-12387"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "55cd2fdb-4cae-5f0b-bea0-e845d51190e1" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186049883}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186198602} {:db/id 17592186198605} {:db/id 17592186278512} {:db/id 17592186278515} {:db/id 17592186278516} {:db/id 17592186278519} {:db/id 17592186373979} {:db/id 17592186401240} {:db/id 17592186401247} {:db/id 17592186401254}] :knowledge-point/title "Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral Using a Formula"} :step/id #uuid "4ec0f874-f1a4-5c03-8a41-bf094ee7ee97" :step/math-academy-id 44446 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199282}} {:db/id 17592186199470 :tutorial/content "Let's now derive a general formula for the flux through an *upward-oriented* Cartesian surface.
